* feat(compass-generative-ai): prompt iteration 1 — timestamp-integer guidance

Number-typed fields with timestamp-like names (created, updated, *_at)
were being mapped to date.* methods without sample values, producing
Date objects that violate the declared Number type.

Adds a "Field-Type vs. Field-Name Conflicts" section clarifying that
the declared schema type is authoritative: Number-typed fields must use
number.int even when the name suggests a date.

* refactor(eval): scorer iteration 2 — skip FakerSampleValueAccuracy on no-sample fields

FakerSampleValueAccuracy measures whether the LLM correctly uses sample
values that were *provided*. When a field has no sampleValues the scorer
has nothing to validate the LLM's invented enum array against, so the
old behavior (count the field as failed with reason "no sampleValues for
field") was conflating two different signals:

  1. LLM used wrong arg values given provided samples (real failure)
  2. LLM used arrayElement on a no-sample field (not a failure of the
     sample-value-accuracy property; also often high quality in practice —
     the LLM invents domain-plausible enums like movie genres, country
     names, unit codes)

This commit: skip such fields (do not increment `checked`) so the score
reflects only the first signal. The second signal belongs to
FakerMethodSuggestionAccuracy.

FLAGGED AS A SCORER CHANGE per workflow rules. This tightens the
scorer's semantic scope rather than inflating it. Output quality on
no-sample variants is independently measured by:
 - FakerMethodRunnableScorer (args don't crash the method)
 - FakerMethodSuggestionAccuracy (method choice is reasonable)

* refactor(eval): scorer iteration 3 — accept helpers.arrayElement in GenericStringMethodCriterion

For no-sample-value test variants the LLM frequently picks
helpers.arrayElement and invents a domain-plausible enum from its world
knowledge (e.g. ["Drama","Comedy","Action",...] for a movie genres
field, NOAA coverage terms for weather). Observed outputs are
consistently high-quality — materially better than the lorem.word /
string.alphanumeric alternatives the criterion previously accepted.

This recognizes that strategy as a valid method choice. FakerSampleValueAccuracy
(iteration 2) still protects against junk sampleValue usage when samples
are provided.

* feat(compass-generative-ai): prompt iteration 4 — sample-value-format guidance

Adds precise sample-value-to-method mappings for formats the LLM was
getting wrong:
  - ISO-3166 alpha-2 country codes ('US') → location.countryCode, not
    location.country
  - 2-letter state codes → location.state with {abbreviated:true}
  - 3-letter currency codes → finance.currencyCode
  - All-digit strings → string.numeric, not string.alphanumeric

These addressed the remaining Ecommerce failures after iteration 3
(shippingAddress.country, billingAddress.country, trackingNumber).

company.name, name→commerce.productName/company.catchPhrase,
category→commerce.department). These are higher-quality mock data than

distinct value rather than treated as transient. The field was previously
dropped when shaping collection info and is now surfaced.

feat(databases-collections-list): hide storage size when the server does not report it COMPASS-10970 (#8383)

* fix: hide storage size when the server does not report it COMPASS-10970

Atlas Infinite (disaggregated storage) clusters filter storageSize and
freeStorageSize out of dbStats and $collStats for non-internal users, because
those values describe space in the shared storage layer rather than anything a
customer can act on.

Compass coerced the missing fields to 0, so a database holding 4.6 MB of data
displayed "0 B" of storage and the collection tooltip reported a total/used/free
breakdown of three zeros. The $collStats pipeline compounded it: $sum over
$toDouble turns a missing field into 0, so absence was already lost inside the
aggregation. Carry $type probes alongside the accumulators, which have to stay
$sum to add up per-shard values, and keep the fields undefined when absent.

Decide what to display from the data rather than from the cluster type: drop the
storage size column when no row whose stats were fetched reports a value. Normal
clusters are untouched, and no cluster-type detection is needed - which matters
because a client cannot identify a disaggregated cluster for every user role.
Rows that are still loading keep the column so the layout does not shift, rows
whose stats could not be fetched do not influence the decision, and views are
excluded because they never report a storage size.

feat(compass-query-bar): drag a field from a document onto the query bar filter (#8459)

* feat(compass-components): drag a field from a document to copy it

Field names in the document view are now drag sources. Dragging one puts
"field: value" (shell syntax) on the drag data, so it can be dropped into
the query bar, an aggregation stage, or any editor outside Compass,
instead of going through the context menu and a separate paste.

The payload is deliberately the same string the existing "Copy field &
value" context menu action writes to the clipboard, so the two ways of
copying a field cannot drift apart. That menu also remains the keyboard
accessible path, since drag and drop is pointer only.

Only the field name is a drag source, not the whole row, so selecting
text in a value still works. Dragging is disabled while a document is
being edited, where the key is a text input.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(compass-query-bar): drop a dragged field onto the filter to add it

Dragging a field already carried "field: value" as text. It now also
carries the field path and value in structured form, and the filter
input accepts it as a drop target: dropping a field adds it to the
current filter instead of pasting its text.

Fields accumulate rather than replace, which is the point of dragging
several of them. A filter with two keys is an implicit $and, and
dropping the same field twice collects the values into an $in. This is
done by dispatching the same addDistinctValue change the "Add to query"
context menu already uses, so the two entry points cannot diverge.

Values travel as canonical extended JSON. That keeps ObjectId, Date and
Decimal128 intact, and keeps 64 bit integers exact, which relaxed mode
would silently round past 2^53. It also matches what the context menu
passes today, since hadron-document holds numbers as BSON numeric types.

The drop is handled in the capture phase because the editor has its own
drop handling that would otherwise insert the plain text version first.
Only the filter accepts field drops; sort and project do not.
